text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) parliamentary deputies calling for an investigation into the "wheat" scandal.
- Croatia to regain authority in the Danube region in the Spring.
- 105 bodies of Moslems killed at the beginning of the war in Bosnia unearthed near Kljuc and another 150 near Srebrenica.
- Money market: Lending rates could go up if poor bank liquidity continues.
- The government will set bread prices, which will be marginally lower than the current ones, says in an interview assistant economy minister, Branko Jordanic.
- 700 war invalids awaiting to be sacked.

- If the current trend of monthly inflation, which was 0.3 percent in September continues Croatia could end the year with a 3.0 annual inflation placing it in the rank of the most developed countries.
- Although Zagrebacka Banka brokers are topping the Zagreb Bourse activities, the presence of small shareholders is on the rise.
- Levi's to decide in the next three months whether it will renew its contract with Varteks, says the Varteks company's Jeans division director, Davor Darabos.
- The National Bank governor Marko Skreb: Croatia's relations with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) are excellent!
- Five U.S. touroperators have included Croatia in their 1997 catalogues. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
